Read-only research in /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa. DO NOT run any contentful CLI, npm script, or read .env/.env.shared/.env.<tier> files (.env.sample is fine). Do not edit anything.

Search the `.docs/` tree (and `.claude/` rules, and `CODEOWNERS`) for everything about Contentful. I need, quoted with file:line:

1. Any documented policy/procedure about which Contentful environment to run tooling against first (e.g. "always run against a non-production environment first"), who owns `scripts/contentful/`, and any approval gate.
2. The documented Contentful environment topology / tier mapping (dev/test/sit/staging/uat/master + `production` alias), and any statement about the `master` environment or the production alias being live/production.
3. Anything documenting content promotion, entry seeding, content migration between environments, or use of `contentful-export` / `contentful-import` / `contentful-cli` / `space export` / backups.
4. Anything about Contentful locales, the `en-CA` locale, or a locale back-fill / re-run of `bootstrapSpace.mjs`. Include any memory/state docs (`.docs/memory/*.md`) mentioning Contentful, test tier, or SFCC-55 footer content.
5. Anything about the Contentful webhook → MRT cache purge (CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET), and anything about a Contentful "Experience"/Studio Experiences content type needing to exist in an environment.
6. Any note about what the deployed test tier currently points at (CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID for test) and any known issue about test having no content.

Report exact quotes with absolute file paths and line numbers. Be thorough — check `.docs/integration/`, `.docs/prd/`, `.docs/memory/`, `.docs/architecture.md`, `.docs/*.md`, `CODEOWNERS`, and `.github/workflows/` for Contentful references. Do not summarise away specifics; I need the literal wording of any policy sentence.

137 .docs/integration/02-contentful.md
     1	# 02 — Contentful (CMS)
     2	
     3	## 1. Purpose and scope
     4	
     5	Contentful is the headless CMS for editorial content: homepage modules, promotional banners, lookbooks, campaign landing pages, size guide fallback content (primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay — PRD-053), footer, and editorial blocks on PLPs and PDPs. The storefront reads published content via the **Delivery API (CDA)** from both SSR and the browser, reads draft content via the **Preview API (CPA)** in editor sessions, and receives **publish webhooks** to clear the SSR cache.
     6	
     7	In scope:
     8	
     9	- Reading published content via the Delivery API
    10	- Reading draft content via the Preview API in editor preview sessions
    11	- Live preview in Contentful Studio
    12	- Locale-specific content via Contentful's native localisation
    13	- Contentful Studio Experiences — drag-and-drop page composition by editors
    14	- Receiving publish webhooks to clear stale SSR cache entries
    15	
    16	Out of scope of this document:
    17	
    18	- Content type schema sync (managed in code via the Management API — see §2)
    19	- Asset uploads and content editing in Contentful Studio
    20	- Webhooks from Contentful to SFCC (none planned)
    21	
    22	**Content ownership.** SFCC owns all commerce data; Contentful owns editorial. On pages that mix both, editorial comes from Contentful and commerce data is resolved from SFCC. Product and category references in Contentful entries are authored via the Salesforce Commerce Cloud Connector app and resolved at render (HPC-001). Rows marked *pending* are unconfirmed (see §11).
    23	
    24	| Surface | SFCC owns | Contentful owns | Status |
    25	|---|---|---|---|
    26	| Homepage | Commerce data for embedded product refs | All modules — hero, banners, campaign blocks | Confirmed |
    27	| Campaign landing pages | Commerce data for embedded product refs | Full page (Contentful Studio Experiences) | Confirmed |
    28	| Lookbooks | Commerce data for shop-the-look refs | Imagery, layout, copy | Confirmed |
    29	| Size guides | — | Fallback content only — primary size guide is the Measmerize overlay (PRD-053, confirmed 2026-06-19); Contentful serves size guide content only where no Measmerize data exists for a given product | Updated |
    30	| Footer | — | All content | Confirmed |
    31	| PLP / category | Category results, product tiles, facets, pagination, hero/banner and editorial rows (SFCC BM — SPR-03/04/64) | Contentful-authored editorial rows, if any | *Whether any PLP editorial comes from Contentful is pending* |
    32	| PDP | Product attributes, price, inventory, variations, gallery | Marketing copy, editorial blocks, size guide fallback (primary size guide is Measmerize — PRD-053) | *Which blocks are Contentful vs SFCC Page Designer is pending* |
    33	| Navigation / mega-menu | Category tree | Promotional tiles, if any | *Pending* |
    34	| Product badges | Badge labels and taxonomy — managed in SFCC BM product attributes (PRD-005); clickable badges link to category/PLP. Contentful is not the source of badge content unless explicitly confirmed. | — | Confirmed |
    35	
    36	## 2. Content type management (build-time)
    37	
    38	Content type schemas are managed in code, not in the Contentful UI:
    39	
    40	- Schema definitions live in the PWA repo and are reviewed via pull request.
    41	- A sync script (Management API) idempotently upserts content types into the target environment. The sync script is authored to be additive only — it never deletes a field from a live content type.
    42	- Each content type pairs with a typed React component. TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time.
    43	
    44	## 3. Browser-side architecture
    45	
    46	```
    47	PWA (SSR layer, then CSR hydration)
    48	        │
    49	        ├──► Contentful Delivery API (CDA) — published content
    50	        │        SSR fetches server-side; browser also uses CDA on
    51	        │        post-hydration reads. Public token, safe in bundle.
    52	        │
    53	        ├──► Contentful Preview API (CPA) — draft content
    54	        │        Editor preview only. Token set in MRT as an env var
    55	        │        on dev/test/sit/uat only (never staging or prod).
    56	        │        Reached client-side on the /preview route and via
    57	        │        ?preview on Experience pages — both are gated: if no
    58	        │        CPA token is present, both paths fail explicitly with
    59	        │        a 404 and are noindex (no delivery fallback). The Live
    60	        │        Preview SDK requires the token in the browser for
    61	        │        postMessage-based real-time updates.
    62	        │
    63	        ├──► Contentful Images API (images.ctfassets.net)
    64	        │        srcset / sizes / avif|webp / quality parameters
    65	        │
    66	        └──◄  Publish webhook → MRT /webhooks/contentful
    67	                 Clears affected SSR cache keys on entry publish.
    68	                 HMAC-verified with a shared secret.
    69	```
    70	
    71	- **SSR first.** Editorial content for SEO- and LCP-critical pages (homepage, PLP, PDP, campaign landings) is fetched server-side. The browser hydrates from the SSR payload — no CDA call on first paint.
    72	- **GraphQL for composed pages.** Where a page assembles many entries the storefront uses the GraphQL Content API to fetch only the needed fields in one request. REST CDA is used for simpler reads.
    73	- **Live preview.** When an editor opens preview in Contentful Studio, the `/preview` route renders the entry inside Studio's iframe. The `@contentful/live-preview` SDK subscribes to `postMessage` events from Studio for real-time content updates. The CPA token is used client-side here — this is required by the SDK and is acceptable because: (a) the token is set only on dev/test/sit/uat (never staging or prod) MRT environments, (b) the route returns a 404 when no preview token is present, and (c) the route is `noindex`. The MRT proxy approach was considered but deferred in favour of the simpler client-side SDK integration.
    74	- **Asset delivery.** Images come from `images.ctfassets.net`. The storefront generates `srcset`, `sizes`, AVIF with WebP fallback, and quality parameters per breakpoint.
    75	
    76	## 4. Authentication and credentials
    77	
    78	| Token | Where used | Sensitivity |
    79	|---|---|---|
    80	| Delivery API token (CDA) | Browser bundle and SSR | Public — read-only, scoped to one environment. Safe to embed. |
    81	| Preview API token (CPA) | `/preview` route and `?preview` on Experience pages (dev/test/sit/uat only — never staging or prod) | Semi-sensitive — exposes drafts. Set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only; never set on staging or prod. Both the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages return 404 and are `noindex` when the token is absent — they fail explicitly, with no delivery fallback. Used client-side by the Live Preview SDK (required for postMessage updates). |
    82	| Management API token (CMA) | Build-time schema sync script | High. Held on the CI host only. Never embedded. |
    83	| Webhook shared secret | MRT webhook receiver | High. Verifies HMAC on inbound publish webhooks. MRT environment variable. |
    84	
    85	Each environment has its own CDA, CPA, and webhook-secret values. The CMA token is per-Space and held only on the CI host.
    86	
    87	## 5. Data exchanged
    88	
    89	| Direction | Data | Mechanism |
    90	|---|---|---|
    91	| Storefront → Contentful | Content type ID, locale, filters, GraphQL query | CDA / Preview API HTTPS GET |
    92	| Contentful → Storefront | JSON entries with resolved linked references | CDA / Preview API response |
    93	| Contentful → Storefront (assets) | Image and video asset URLs | Images API |
    94	| Contentful Studio ↔ PWA iframe | Live preview update events | Cross-origin `postMessage` |
    95	| Contentful → MRT | Publish webhook with entry ID, content type, locale, environment | HTTPS POST with HMAC signature |
    96	
    97	No PII flows through Contentful.
    98	
    99	## 6. Performance and loading strategy
   100	
   101	- **SSR cache.** Contentful responses are cached at the SSR/edge layer — TTL 60 seconds with stale-while-revalidate. Publish webhooks clear the cache; the TTL is the fallback.
   102	- **CDN rate limits.** Contentful allows 55 uncached requests per second per CDA token. The SSR cache absorbs almost all traffic so this limit is only a risk during burst republish events.
   103	- **Images.** AVIF with WebP fallback via the Images API. Lazy loading on all below-the-fold images. The largest hero carries `fetchpriority="high"`.
   104	- **Preconnect.** `images.ctfassets.net` is preconnected from the document head. `cdn.contentful.com` is not — first paint hydrates from SSR, so no browser CDA call is on the critical path.
   105	- **Bundle weight.** The rich-text renderer is dynamically imported only on pages that use rich-text fields.
   106	- **Field projection.** GraphQL queries select only the fields the component uses. REST queries use the `select` parameter where supported.
   107	
   108	## 7. Multi-region behaviour
   109	
   110	- A single Contentful Space serves all eight storefronts via Contentful's native locale model.
   111	- The active locale is resolved from the URL prefix and passed as `locale=` on every CDA request. Eleven active locales: en-AU, en-US, en-GB, en (EU), fr, it, es, en-CH, en-HK, en-AE.
   112	- Region-specific entries (banners, promotions, editorial that varies by site) are filtered at query time using the active SFCC site ID.
   113	
   114	## 8. Failure modes and graceful degradation
   115	
   116	| Failure | Behaviour |
   117	|---|---|
   118	| Contentful CDA unavailable | Page renders without editorial content. Editorial slots show empty; commerce data is never blocked on a CMS read. |
   119	| Stale cached content after a publish | Tolerated within the 60-second TTL. The publish webhook normally clears affected entries in seconds; the TTL is the safety net if the webhook drops. |
   120	| Preview API returns broken or unpublished refs | Editor preview only — render a placeholder. Production traffic never hits this path. |
   121	| Asset (image) 404 | Show alt text and a graceful placeholder. |
   122	| 429 rate limit on CDA | Exponential backoff and retry. The SSR cache makes this rare in practice. |
   123	| Publish webhook fails HMAC verification | Reject and log. Storefront continues serving from cache; the TTL picks up the change. |
   124	| Live preview iframe disconnects | Storefront silently returns to non-preview mode. |
   125	
   126	## 9. Security and privacy
   127	
   128	- The CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment. Embedding in the bundle is safe per Contentful's published guidance.
   129	- The CPA token is set in MRT on dev/test/sit/uat only — never on staging or prod. It reaches the browser on the `/preview` route and `?preview` Experience pages, both of which return 404 when no token is present. Both preview paths are `noindex` and not linked from any storefront navigation. This is a deliberate tradeoff: the Live Preview SDK requires the token client-side for real-time postMessage updates, and the non-prod-only gate means the token is never in a production bundle.
   130	- The CMA token is held only on the CI host — never embedded, never in PR diffs.
   131	- No PII is handled by Contentful.
   132	
   133	## 10. Open items requiring client confirmation
   134	
   135	1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
   136	2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC owns all commerce data, Contentful owns editorial. Not yet confirmed is the split on composed pages: which editorial blocks appear on PDP and PLP, whether they are authored in SFCC Page Designer or Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or built in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu includes Contentful-authored promotional tiles. The working assumption is in the ownership table in §1.
   137	3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provide per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be tested against a real Contentful environment.

Both live in your local, gitignored `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold them, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running). Get the management token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.

Ongoing product sync via MuleSoft post-migration. **DMU-002 — Confirmed (status flipped from Ready for Sign Off, 2026-06-11).** The PWA-side contract is settled: SFCC displays exactly what MuleSoft returns for product data (JT 04-06), with AP21 as the master of record. .docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md:11:- Product feed via MuleSoft from AP21 to SFCC covering ~1,600 active SKUs: names, descriptions, attributes, imagery refs, category assignments (DMU-001). .docs/prd/dataMigrationSeo.md:14:- **Customer passwords are not migrated** — customers must reset on first login (DMU-005). See AGENTS.md "Magento password migration" gotcha.

.docs/architecture.md:195:**Experience Builder components** (drag-and-drop in Contentful Studio) are a separate concern — they are registered in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` and do not need a corresponding content-type entry unless they also have a standard content type for use outside Studio.

Content types are managed via `npm run sync:contentful` — see Contentful Content Type Management below. Cache invalidation on entry publish via a Contentful → MRT webhook, HMAC-verified with `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
.docs/temp/openItems.md:53:2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
.docs/temp/openItems.md:60:3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
.docs/temp/openItems.md:155:2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

164:each environment — Contentful's current recommended mechanism, replacing an earlier
170:- `scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js` — assembles every content type in the definitions directory into one `EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`
171:- `scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs` — validates then installs the template's current version into one target environment

Both live in your local, gitignored `.env.shared` (never commit; run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold them, then `npm run env -- <tier>` to activate a tier before running). Get the management token from `app.contentful.com/account/profile/cma_tokens`. `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` is shared across tiers; `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` is set per tier and auto-fetched by `npm run env -- init` once the management token is filled in.

263:Only **email + Omneo customer ID** are migrated into SFCC at go-live. All other customer profile data — name, phone, addresses, communication preferences — is sourced **live from Omneo at login** via MuleSoft. Implication: My Account profile pages cannot rely on SFCC for the full customer record; an Omneo round-trip is required post-authentication. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages becomes load-bearing on account screens. Asset/CDN migration (DMU-010) is **de-scoped** — images stay in Contentful, no asset 301s.
267:Multiple upstream integrations (SFCC, MuleSoft/Omneo, Global-e, Narvar, Contentful, Didomi, Inside Chat) mean a failure or attack targeting one service must not cascade. A PWA-relevant mitigation can be done in the SSR layer.
269:The SSR layer in `overrides/app/ssr.js` uses **Node's native `fetch`**, which is backed by `undici`. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).

93:    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). 85:- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
86:- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
87:- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
88:  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
89:  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
90:  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
91:  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
92:    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
93:    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
94:    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
95:    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
96:    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
97:  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
98:    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
99:    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.

=== architecture.md 85-135 ===
85:### External services
86:
87:Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Contentful Studio CMS, Global-e (international checkout + server-side pricing/catalogue feed — PRC-34..43 sign-off pending), Didomi (consent), GTM hosted on Addingwell (data layer + downstream tag loading via Tell No Lies). Full integration map below.
88:
89:## Environments
90:
91:Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).
92:
93:| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
94:| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
95:| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
96:| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
97:| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
98:| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
99:| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
100:| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |
101:
102:**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).
103:
104:**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.
105:
106:**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.
107:
108:**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | uat | stage | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.
109:
110:## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
111:
112:Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.
113:
114:## Overrides Pattern
115:
116:All customizations live in `overrides/` mirroring the structure of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/`. Never edit `node_modules/`.
117:
118:**Minimise custom code.** When implementing Zimmermann's design and layout, stay as close to the base PWA Kit implementation as possible. Style changes (CSS, Chakra props, theme tokens) are always expected and need no confirmation. Structural changes — restructuring components, altering data flow, or significantly deviating from base template behaviour — must be confirmed with the user before proceeding.
119:
120:**Before any change:** check whether the file exists in `overrides/`. If not, create the override:
121:
122:1. Copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/`.
123:2. Rename `.js`/`.jsx` → `.ts`/`.tsx`. Replace `PropTypes` with TypeScript `type` definitions. Add explicit types to all parameters, return values, and props. Use Commerce SDK types (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`, `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react`) where available. No `as any` or `// @ts-ignore`.
124:3. Verify `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with zero errors.
125:4. **Stop. Present the converted file to the user and wait for approval before making any functional changes.**
126:
127:## New vs. Override Components
128:
129:- **Overriding a base template component:** copy from `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` to the mirrored path in `overrides/` (see Overrides Pattern above).
130:- **Brand-new components** (no base template equivalent): create them in `overrides/app/components/custom/`.
131:
132:## Key Paths
133:
134:- **Country/locale/currency mappings:** `overrides/app/config/countries.ts` — single source of truth for URL slugs, locales, currencies, shipping countries, Global-e flag, and boutique regions. When adding a market also update `config/sites.js`.
135:- **Contentful config:** `overrides/app/config/contentful.ts` — always render locale-specific content using Contentful's native localisation fields. Gate preview/draft content behind a server-side check; never expose draft content in production.

129:- **Environment variables:** Never hardcode secrets, tokens, API keys, or credentials anywhere in the codebase. Local values live in `.env.shared` (tier-independent) and `.env.<tier>` (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod) — gitignored, managed via `npm run env` (`scripts/switchEnv.mjs`; full command reference in `.env.sample`'s header) — and are set as platform environment variables on Managed Runtime for staging/prod. When adding a new env var: (1) add it to `.env.sample` tagged `# scope:shared|tier|personal|auto` on its own comment line above the key (value only if it's a non-secret public identifier, otherwise leave blank — never a trailing comment, or a blank placeholder reads as non-empty to the pre-commit secret guard), (2) run `npm run env -- init` to scaffold the new key into `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>`, then fill in the real value locally. Never put tokens, bearer credentials, DSNs, or licence keys in `.env.sample`. Non-personal shared/tier values may additionally be centrally published via `npm run env -- push <scope>` (tier-1-approvers only) to this repo's GitHub Environments — genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal`, e.g. your own Atlassian or Contentful CMA token) must never be pushed.

     1	# Contentful tooling
     2	
     3	Zimmermann uses **two different Contentful surfaces**. Keep them straight — they live in different places and are managed by different tools.
     4	
     5	## 1. Content types (editorial schemas)
     6	
     7	**What:** Schemas for editorial entries authors fill in (e.g. `footerConfig`, `link`).
     8	**Where:** `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` — plain JS, one file per content type. This is the **sole** source of truth for a content type's fields, including `required`/`localized`/`validations` — there is no separate migration file layered on top.
     9	**How:** Pushed as one organization-scoped **Environment Template**, then installed into each environment. This is Contentful's current recommended mechanism — content models are authored once at the organization level, not created independently per space/environment (see the `contentful-management` SDK's `client.environmentTemplate.*` API).
    10	
    11	```bash
    12	npm run sync:contentful                                   # build/update the template from content-types/*.js
    13	npm run install:contentful -- --target dev                # push it into one environment
    14	npm run install:contentful -- --target dev --dry-run       # validate only, no changes
    15	```
    16	
    17	Driven by [buildTemplate.js](./buildTemplate.js) (assembles `content-types/*.js` into one
    18	`EnvironmentTemplate`, get-or-created by name under `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`) and
    19	[setup/installTemplate.mjs](./setup/installTemplate.mjs) (validates then installs the
    20	template's current version into `--target <environmentId>`, polling until the install
    21	reaches a terminal status). Reads `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID`,
    22	and `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` from `.env`.
    23	
    24	Promotion order: `dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master` — run `install:contentful`
    25	against each target in turn. Contentful tracks each environment's install status/version
    26	natively (`environmentTemplateInstallation`) — there's no hand-rolled migration-history
    27	content type and no separate drift-detection script, since every environment installs
    28	from the same versioned template and can't drift from it the way independently-synced
    29	environments used to.
    30	
    31	**Entries are a separate concern from the template.** Environment Templates cover
    32	content-*type* schema only — seed data (e.g. the canonical `region` entries) needs its
    33	own per-environment script, run after that environment has the relevant content type
    34	installed:
    35	
    36	```bash
    37	npm run seed:contentful-regions -- --target dev
    38	```
    39	
    40	See [setup/seedRegions.mjs](./setup/seedRegions.mjs).
    41	
    42	To add a new content type: drop a new file in [content-types/](./content-types/) following
    43	the shape of [footerConfig.js](./content-types/footerConfig.js) (explicit `localized`
    44	per field), then re-run `sync:contentful` followed by `install:contentful` per environment.
    45	
    46	## 2. Studio Experiences component definitions (visual builder)
    47	
    48	**What:** Registers Zimmermann React components with Contentful Studio Experiences so authors can drop them onto pages in the visual builder.
    49	**Where:** `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/` — one `.tsx` per component, plus a single generated `definitions.ts` registry.
    50	**How:** Imported at runtime by `defineComponents` — no push step. The registry is **generated from code**; never edit `definitions.ts` by hand.
    51	
    52	### Author workflow
    53	
    54	1. Create or update your component in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/`.
    55	2. Add `/** @cf-register */` immediately before the component's `const` declaration.
    56	3. Annotate every prop in the `Props` type with a `@cf` JSDoc tag:
    57	
    58	   ```tsx
    59	   type MyComponentProps = {
    60	     /** @cf Headline */
    61	     headline: string;
    62	
    63	     /** @cf Hero Image, media */
    64	     heroImage?: string;
    65	
    66	     /** @cf skip */
    67	     internalId?: string;
    68	   };
    69	   ```
    70	
    71	4. Run the generator:
    72	
    73	   ```bash
    74	   npm run generate:contentful
    75	   ```
    76	
    77	   This rewrites `definitions.ts` automatically. Commit both the annotated component and the updated `definitions.ts`.
    78	
    79	5. The pre-commit hook runs the generator automatically when an `experiences/*.tsx` file is staged, keeping `definitions.ts` in sync.
    80	
    81	For full tag syntax and control options, see the `/contentful-register-component` skill.
    82	
    83	### CI check
    84	
    85	```bash
    86	npm run generate:contentful:check
    87	```
    88	
    89	Exits zero if `definitions.ts` is up to date, non-zero (with a diff) if regeneration is needed. Wire into CI to catch a forgotten regenerate.
    90	
    91	## Don't cross the streams
    92	
    93	- A Studio Experiences component (`experiences/*.tsx`) does **not** belong in [content-types/](./content-types/) — `buildTemplate.js` does not understand it.
    94	- A content-type definition (`content-types/*.js`) does **not** belong in `experiences/` — it is an API artefact, not a runtime component.
    95	- **Never edit `definitions.ts` directly.** The file is autogenerated; manual edits will be overwritten on the next run.

=== deploy-test.yml ===
     1	name: Deploy Test
     2	
     3	on:
     4	  workflow_dispatch:
     5	    inputs:
     6	      ref:
     7	        description: 'Branch or tag to deploy (e.g. feature/my-story, or a release tag)'
     8	        required: true
     9	        default: 'develop'
    10	      rollback:
    11	        description: 'Authorised rollback — skip the downgrade guard to deploy an older, known-good tag'
    12	        type: boolean
    13	        default: false
    14	
    15	permissions:
    16	  contents: read
    17	  id-token: write
    18	  deployments: write
    19	
    20	# Serialise deploys to this environment so two runs can't both pass the version
    21	# check and then land out of order (which would downgrade the environment).
    22	concurrency:
    23	  group: deploy-test
    24	  cancel-in-progress: false
    25	
    26	jobs:
    27	  deploy-test:
    28	    name: Deploy to Test
    29	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    30	    environment: test
    31	    outputs:
    32	      # Commit the deployed build was made from. The post-deploy gate pins to
    33	      # this so it measures the exact revision that landed on Test, even when
    34	      # `ref` is a mutable branch that moves between the two jobs' checkouts.
    35	      sha: ${{ steps.resolve-sha.outputs.sha }}
    36	    env:
    37	      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
    38	      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    39	    steps:
    40	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    41	        with:
    42	          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}
    43	
    44	      - name: Resolve deployed commit SHA
    45	        id: resolve-sha
    46	        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
    47	
    48	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    49	        with:
    50	          node-version: '24'
    51	          cache: 'npm'
    52	
    53	      - name: Install dependencies
    54	        run: npm install --include=dev
    55	
    56	      - name: Guard against version downgrade
    57	        if: ${{ inputs.rollback != true }}
    58	        env:
    59	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    60	          DEPLOY_REF: ${{ inputs.ref }}

=== tsd-architecture contentful ===
16:- Integration map (SFCC, MuleSoft, Contentful, Global-e, Didomi, Adyen, Omneo, Narvar, GiveX, Google Places)
30:The PWA itself also talks to a handful of services without going through SFCC. Contentful and Didomi are browser-direct. Google Maps (Places API), GiveX balance check (proxied through MuleSoft — see §2 GiveX note), and select MuleSoft operations are called from the PWA's MRT Node layer via proxy, with API credentials held server-side as MRT environment variables.
44:   PWA Kit (Managed Runtime)       • Contentful                       Global-e
96:- **PWA → Contentful, Vimeo, Didomi, GTM (via Addingwell), Optimizely Web, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, Narvar Promise, Adyen Drop-In, Measmerize:** browser-direct; no SFCC involvement. GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Inside Chat, and Narvar Promise load post-Didomi-consent only.
152:| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID`, `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Contentful Delivery API (published content)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Browser + SSR. CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle but held as an MRT env var so rotation is centralised                                       |
153:| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN`, `CONTENTFUL_HOST`                                   | Contentful Preview API (drafts, editor sessions)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | MRT-mediated — proxied server-side; never reaches the browser                                                                                                                   |
154:| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`                                                   | Contentful Management API (schema sync)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | **Local / CI only** — never deployed to MRT                                                                                                                                     |
155:| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`                                                            | Shared secret for the Contentful → MRT cache-purge webhook (HMAC verification)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | MRT-mediated                                                                                                                                                                    |
173:- Non-personal shared/tier values can be centrally published and pulled via this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per deployment tier under Settings > Environments), stored as GitHub Environment Variables — write access requires repo Admin (`@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`), read access is repo-collaborator-wide. This is a deliberate, documented exception to using GitHub Secrets (which cannot be read back via API once set) — see `.env.sample`'s header for the full rationale. Genuinely personal credentials (`scope:personal` — your own Jira/Confluence token, your own Contentful CMA token) are always excluded from this and never centralized.
257:| **Contentful — Delivery (CDA)**                | Published editorial content (on live website)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | MRT + Browser                                                                                                                                                          | Browser-direct + MRT-mediated                    | CDA token is read-only and scoped to one environment; safe in bundle. SSR-first for SEO/LCP, browser hydration uses the SSR payload                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
258:| **Contentful — Preview (CPA)**                 | Editor preview sessions, draft content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | MRT (SSR pass and editor proxy)                                                                                                                                        | MRT-mediated                                     | CPA token is semi-sensitive (exposes drafts); held server-side and proxied through MRT — never reaches the browser                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
259:| **Contentful — Management (CMA)**              | Schema sync (`npm run sync:contentful`), Studio editor OAuth                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Out-of-band (CI host)                                                                                                                                                  | Out-of-band                                      | CMA token never embedded; stored as a CI environment variable on the host that runs the sync                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
260:| **Contentful publish webhook**                 | Cache invalidation on entry publish                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Contentful → MRT                                                                                                                                                       | MRT-mediated                                     | Webhook receiver in the Node/SSR layer; shared-secret HMAC verification on the incoming request                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
261:| **Vimeo**                                      | Product video hosting — PDP gallery, runway / campaign clips (PRD-066/067)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Browser (lazy iframe embed)                                                                                                                                            | Browser-direct                                   | Embed URL stored in product data or the CMS; no secret. Loaded behind a facade (poster image + click/scroll-to-load) so the Vimeo player JS stays off the LCP critical path. Editorial-page video is Contentful by default but may also embed Vimeo by URL (HPC-004). PRD-067 (Vimeo as the chosen platform) still Open                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
286:| **Transperfect**                               | Translation pipeline for Contentful (REG-047)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Contentful ↔ Transperfect directly                                                                                                                                     | Out-of-band                                      | No PWA involvement                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
289:| **Measmerize**                                 | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP (PRD-050–053). The PWA injects the Measmerize script on PDP and passes the product identifier. The widget self-determines whether it has data for the product and signals the PWA accordingly — the PWA either shows the Find My Size trigger or falls back to the Contentful size guide. Widget configuration, size guide content, and recommendation logic are owned by Measmerize / Zimmermann. | Browser (PDP only)                                                                                                                                                     | Browser-direct                                   | Public identifier in bundle; no secret. Script defers behind LCP. **Consent approach unconfirmed — open item.**                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
292:### 7.3 Contentful schema as code
295:organization-scoped Contentful Environment Template (`npm run sync:contentful`), then
296:installed into each environment (`npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>`) using a
297:Contentful Management Token — Contentful's current recommended mechanism for content
301:Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module.
379:- **Images:** all storefront imagery — product and editorial — is stored in and served from **Contentful** (`images.ctfassets.net`) via the Contentful Images API; SFCC holds no image assets (DMU-010 migration de-scoped; product images CRM-075; all media via the CMS library HPC-003). The PWA generates `srcset` / `sizes` and sets size, quality, and format per breakpoint on the asset URL — **AVIF primary with WebP / JPEG fallbacks**. Lazy-load all non-LCP images; priority-load the primary hero image (PRD-064). Never render full-resolution images at thumbnail size.
382:  - **Content-managed page videos → Contentful** by default, served from the Contentful asset CDN and referenced within the CMS content entry alongside the page content. Editorial pages may also embed a Vimeo video by URL where preferred (HPC-004) — the product/editorial split above is the expected pattern, not a hard restriction.
428:- Localised privacy policy pages, served from Contentful per storefront.
458:| Contentful               | Render page without editorial content; never block commerce data on CMS                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
478:`overrides/app/ssr.js` makes server-side `fetch` calls directly (token exchange, JWKS, SF Payments metadata). Node's native `fetch` is backed by `undici` internally. Undici's `dispatcher` option (the per-call `dispatcher` option on individual `fetch()` invocations) allows each upstream origin to be given its own connection pool with an independent cap. This prevents a slow or flooded integration (e.g. checkout APIs) from exhausting connections for unrelated origins (e.g. Contentful, JWKS).
494:**Contentful:** The Contentful SDK (`contentful` v11) does not expose a `dispatcher` hook on its internal fetch calls, so connection isolation for Contentful is not achievable through this pattern. Primary mitigation is the graceful degradation rule in §12 (Render page without editorial content).
510:Failure paths that would be non-obvious or costly to debug: Contentful → component data mapping, locale / currency transforms, Global-e pricing / tax branching, checkout ownership, consent gating, cart mutations, optimistic-update rollback. Framework behaviour and pure visual rendering are not tested at this layer.
532:A six-tier environment topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).

292:### 7.3 Contentful schema as code
293:
294:Content type definitions live in version control and are authored as one
295:organization-scoped Contentful Environment Template (`npm run sync:contentful`), then
296:installed into each environment (`npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>`) using a
297:Contentful Management Token — Contentful's current recommended mechanism for content
298:models, replacing an earlier per-environment sync script. Field deletion on install is
299:opt-in and off by default. Each definition pairs with a typed React component, so schema
300:changes are reviewable and repeatable. Experience Builder components (drag-and-drop in
301:Contentful Studio) are registered through a separate registration module.
302:
303:### 7.4 Non-system stakeholders
304:
305:Parties that influence the build but are not systems the storefront integrates with at runtime. Their deliverables hand over to Accenture for implementation.
306:
307:| Party                                          | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Handover to Accenture                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
308:| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
309:| **Sparro**                                     | External SEO consultancy. Defines the JSON-LD schema templates (PDP, PLP, boutique, homepage — DMU-037 to DMU-040), the consolidated hreflang structure (DMU-025), and the CMS-editable on-page SEO field schema (DMU-035).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Specification documents per requirement ID; Accenture implements in SFCC / PWA. Final JSON-LD scope and page types to be confirmed before build (DMU-038).                                                                                                                                                |
310:| **Accessibility vendor** _(TBC by Zimmermann)_ | Manual accessibility audits, screen-reader and assistive-tech testing, audit cadence, remediation triage. Complements the automated coverage in §10.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Audit reports per cadence; defects raised back into the Accenture backlog. Vendor name, screen-reader / browser matrix, and cadence still pending from Zimmermann.                                                                                                                                        |

content.content:
=== a3de288 ===
fix(contentful): provision locales before cloning, and back-fill existing environments

`en-CA` was missing from LOCALES, so `/en-ca/` Experience pages send a locale the
space doesn't have and the CDA returns 400 — degrading to "Page not found" on
ZimmermannUSIntl. Adding it alone would not have fixed anything, because the
propagation model was broken underneath.

Locales were created in `master` *after* §1 cloned master into the five target
environments. A clone inherits source locales as they stood at clone time, and
`locale.create` was hardcoded to 'master', so nothing back-filled: a locale added
later reached exactly one environment, and re-running never helped. The section
comment claimed the opposite — "cloned environments inherit them" — which is true
only for locales that already existed when the clone was taken.

Locale provisioning is now `provisionLocales(client, environmentId)`, run against
master before §2 clones, then again across a `provisionable` list afterwards so
environments that pre-dated a locale receive it. Idempotent: verified two chained
runs issue zero writes on the second.

Three defects introduced by the first draft of this change, all found by review
before merge and fixed here:

- `--dry-run` pushed a not-yet-existent environment into `provisionable`; the
  back-fill then read its locales, 404'd outside the try/catch, and exited 1
  before API keys and the production alias were previewed. Dry-run on a fresh
  space was broken in exactly the scenario it exists for.
- `default: true` would have been POSTed to five more live environments. The SDK
  strips `default` on update but sends it verbatim on create, so an environment
  with a different incumbent default risks either rejection or a silent repoint
  of what the CDA returns for unlocalized reads. `default` is now only asserted
  on master; a clone already inherits it, and a pre-existing environment's
  default is not this script's to change.
- Locale failures were caught, warned and swallowed with exit 0. That covered one
  environment before; this change made it six, and failures cascade — if `en`
  fails, the nine locales declaring `fallbackCode: 'en'` fail too. Now exits
  non-zero.

Summary prints a count for `locales.skipped` rather than the list, which reaches
~54 entries in the steady state.

Not run against Contentful. The code is correct; `/en-ca/` stays broken until
someone with space access runs `setup:contentful`.

=== 604ece5 ===
docs: reconcile the bootstrap docs with the re-runnable locale flow

README.md said `setup:contentful` was a "One-time space bootstrap. Never re-run
against an already-set-up space." That now contradicts the design: re-running is
precisely how a newly-added locale reaches environments that already exist, since
a clone only inherits master's locales as they stood at clone time. An operator
following the README would never get `en-CA` back-filled; one following the code
would be doing something the README forbids. Rewritten to describe the idempotent
behaviour, the non-zero exit on locale failure, and the `--dry-run` preview.

projectState.md's open-items note said `bootstrapSpace.mjs` "provisions 9 locales
without `en-CA`" — true this morning, false as of a3de288. Updated, and it keeps
the half that is still open: nothing in the repo confirms whether the *live*
space has `en-CA`. Running `setup:contentful` is what would settle it, and until
someone does, `/en-ca/` Experience pages still send an unknown locale to the CDA.

=== 2f8c1f9 ===
fix(contentful): close the validation gate on every unresolved finding

The gate read `!(conflictingIds.length && TAKEOVER_IDS.length)` — "is there at
least one conflict and at least one takeover?" rather than "is every finding
accounted for?". Any single `--takeover` therefore opened it for every *other*
finding too: conflicts the flag never named, and findings of unrelated classes.
`ValidationFinding.message` is typed as an open string in the SDK, so the class
set isn't bounded by the one this code handles.

Three reachable holes, all now refused: one conflict plus one unrelated finding
with the conflict named; three conflicts with only one named; and a conflict with
a typo'd takeover id.

Replaced with an explicit unresolved set — a finding is resolved only if it is a
`conflictingContentTypes` whose `details.contentTypeId` appears in `--takeover`.
Brute-forced across 780 cases (all subsets of a six-finding universe x six
takeover sets x FORCE): zero cases where the new gate is looser, 234 stricter,
546 identical. An always-proceed mutant was flagged as looser in 138 of those,
confirming the comparator detects looseness before the zero is trusted.

Two supporting fixes:

- The new unknown-takeover warning said "adopting nothing for them" while the
  payload was still built from all of TAKEOVER_IDS, so a typo'd id was still
  POSTed as a ContentType link to adopt. Now filtered to ids Contentful actually
  reported as conflicting, making the warning true rather than merely stated.
- `--dry-run` returned before the gate and always printed "Would install", which
  made it useless as a pre-flight for the check this commit strengthens. It now
  reports whether a real run would refuse, and still exits 0.

`--force` behaviour is unchanged and still bypasses the gate entirely. Note it
remains reachable alongside `--delete-deleted-fields` with no allowlist on
`--target`, so `--target master` is accepted — flagged, not addressed here.

Tier 2 (protectedFiles.md, Owner: Integration / SI Partner). Not executed.

=== homepage.md contentful/footer ===
8:The system delivers page templates for the homepage, global navigation, footer, and country/language selector. (Catalogue, cart/checkout, account, content/static, and SEO-migration templates are covered in their own PRDs.)
16:- **Rotating promotional announcement banner** above the header — CMS-managed via Contentful (HPC-017, confirmed).
19:The confirmed header icon set is: **Search, Account, and Bag** (HPC-018). Locate Boutique, Contact Us, and Newsletter are **not part of the header** — confirmed per design review on 23 June 2026. Placement of those three icons elsewhere (footer or other location) remains design-dependent and will follow the new UX designs.
23:- **Country/region selector**: visible in header on all storefronts **except AU** (HPC-026, confirmed — AU is the default/x-default storefront and has no selector). The selector also appears in the **footer**, in addition to the header (HPC-026, confirmed). On mobile it is additionally surfaced within the **hamburger/burger menu** (HPC-025, confirmed). No international pages exist yet (HPC-026 design note). See [regional.md](regional.md) for selector behaviour.
45:- Contentful is the sole CMS across all regional storefronts (HPC-001, confirmed). Integration is via the Salesforce App Exchange connector, consuming content through the Contentful delivery API for all customer-facing pages (Third Party Integrations — CMS / Contentful). Homepage carries product names only, which sit in Contentful.
46:- All images and video assets managed through the **Contentful media library** (HPC-003, confirmed)
55:If Contentful content fails to load, render the page without editorial content — never block on a CMS response. See AGENTS.md Graceful Degradation.
58:- **Contentful vs SFCC scope split** (HPC-001, HPC-002, HPC-006, HPC-010, HPC-012) — pending discussion with Contentful. Affects whether product names/prices sit in Contentful or SFCC ("EK - If we are displaying Product names and Potentially prices this would sit on SFCC").
59:- **Contentful preview environment** (HPC-002) — no primary sign-off; challenged: "EK - As we have a Contentful Studio license - is this required?" Studio licence may make a separate preview environment redundant.
62:- **Reusable page builder templates** (HPC-010) — no primary sign-off; challenged: "is this required? DR: The ability to reuse an existing template is needed... Is this possible within Studio?" Feasibility within Contentful Studio pending.
63:- **Live stream embedding via structured CMS solution** (HPC-012) — no primary sign-off; pending Contentful vs SFCC scope split.
76:## 5. Global Footer (HPC-030 – HPC-033, HPC-038, confirmed)
78:- Global footer with content managed via Contentful, editable per website or locale (HPC-030, confirmed)
79:- Footer navigation links (HPC-031, confirmed) navigate to the relevant page or destination on click (HPC-032, confirmed)
80:- Copyright and legal text in the footer (HPC-033, confirmed)
81:- Business users can add region-specific footer links — e.g. Acknowledgement of Country on AU storefront (HPC-038, confirmed)
82:- **Country/region selector** also appears in the footer (in addition to the header), on all storefronts except AU (HPC-026, confirmed). See section 1 and [regional.md](regional.md).
88:- "Join Us" email capture field in the footer (HPC-034, confirmed)

=== openItems.md contentful ===
22:| 2   | Contentful  | 3                      |
50:## 2. Contentful
53:2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
54:3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.
151:Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.

47:

49:

51:

Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
53:2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). 54:3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.
55:

=== mobify.config.js ===

=== sync-env-vars-to-mrt head ===
     1	name: Sync Env Vars to MRT
     2	
     3	# Reads all keys tagged `mrt:true` in .env.sample, fetches their values from
     4	# the selected GitHub Environment (and the `shared` environment as a fallback)
     5	# via the GitHub API, then PATCHes only the keys that are actually set
     6	# (non-empty) to the MRT target.
     7	#
     8	# Fallback order: target env value → shared env value → skip.
     9	# Keys that exist in .env.sample but are absent from both environments are
    10	# silently skipped — MRT retains whatever value it already holds for them.
    11	#
    12	# CI/tooling vars (CODERABBIT_API_KEY, JIRA_URL, BROWSERSTACK_*, E2E_* etc.)
    13	# are not tagged mrt:true and are never included in the sync.
    14	#
    15	# scope:personal and scope:auto keys (including ENVIRONMENT_NAME) are never
    16	# synced — they are developer-local or script-injected.
    17	#
    18	# ⚠️  PRODUCTION is intentionally excluded from this workflow.
    19	#     Production MRT env vars must be updated manually in the MRT console
    20	#     (runtime.commercecloud.com) by a tier-1-approver. This ensures prod
    21	#     changes go through a human gate rather than an automated workflow.
    22	#
    23	# Trigger: manual only (workflow_dispatch). Run after updating a GitHub
    24	# Environment to propagate new values to MRT without a full redeploy.
    25	
    26	on:
    27	  workflow_dispatch:
    28	    inputs:
    29	      target:
    30	        description: 'MRT target to update (prod excluded — update manually in MRT console)'
    31	        required: true
    32	        type: choice
    33	        options:
    34	          - dev
    35	          - test
    36	          - sit
    37	          - uat
    38	          - staging
    39	      dry_run:
    40	        description: 'Dry run — show what would be synced without calling MRT'
    41	        required: false
    42	        type: boolean
    43	        default: false
    44	
    45	permissions:
    46	  contents: read
    47	
    48	jobs:
    49	  sync:
    50	    name: Sync to MRT (${{ inputs.target }})
    51	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    52	    environment: ${{ inputs.target }}
    53	    env:
    54	      MRT_USER: ${{ secrets.MRT_USER }}
    55	      MRT_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.MRT_API_KEY }}
    56	      MRT_PROJECT: zimmermann
    57	      GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    58	
    59	    steps:
    60	      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

=== README 25-55 (Who legend) ===
25:**Git hooks (Husky):** `pre-commit` blocks committed secrets and warns on Tier 1/2 file changes; `commit-msg` enforces [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format (`type(scope): message`) — a badly formatted message is rejected, not just warned about.
